narration: You probably picture Noah's ark as a wooden ship with animals crowding the deck. But open Genesis, and the description gets more interesting. It specifies rooms, three levels, and pitch on both sides of the wood. Those details change the picture. Detail number one: the rooms. Genesis tells Noah to make rooms inside the ark. Picture a divided interior, rather than one enormous empty space. The passage gives instructions, but it does not show us a complete building plan. Any illustrated arrangement of those compartments is an interpretation. Detail number two: the levels. The text names lower, second, and third stories, and places the door in the side. That means three levels, not simply animals standing beneath a roof. In our drawing, the cutaway makes those levels visible. Their exact internal arrangement remains an illustration, not something recovered from an ancient wreck. Detail number three: the coating. The instruction is to cover the ark within and without with pitch. The inside matters too. Look at a wooden section: the coating belongs on both faces in this explanation, not just the outside of the hull. Now put the details together: a divided interior, three levels, and coating inside and out. We are following a short passage in Genesis, not claiming that a particular modern reconstruction proves exactly how the ark looked. Next time you see an ark illustration, ask three questions. Where are the rooms? Can you see the levels? And what happened to the inside coating?
